storyNotes.originalText: On the way to his uncle, Jacob stopped for the night, using a stone for his PILLOW.
storyNotes.cleanText: On the way to his uncle, Jacob stopped for the night, using a stone for his pillow.

storyNotes.originalText: That night, Jacob dreamed of a STAIRWAY to heaven, with angels going up and down.
storyNotes.cleanText: That night, Jacob dreamed of a stairway to heaven, with angels going up and down.

storyNotes.originalText: God stood at the top of the stairway. He gave Jacob the same PROMISES he made to Abraham.
storyNotes.cleanText: God stood at the top of the stairway. He gave Jacob the same promises he made to Abraham.

storyNotes.originalText: When Jacob woke up, he thought, "God is in this PLACE and I didn't know it!"
storyNotes.cleanText: When Jacob woke up, he thought, "God is in this place and I didn't know it!"

storyNotes.originalText: Jacob stood up the STONE he used for a pillow. He called that place "The House of God."
storyNotes.cleanText: Jacob stood up the stone he used for a pillow. He called that place "The House of God."

questions.question: What was the name of that book?
questions.answer: Genesis.

questions.question: What promises did God give Abraham?
questions.answer: To grow his family into a great nation, give them a great land, and use them to bless the whole world.

questions.question: Who can remind us how that happened?
questions.answer: Jacob disguised himself as his brother, Esau, and fooled his father into giving a prayer of blessing to him instead of his big brother, Esau.

questions.question: What crazy thing was angry Esau ready to do?
questions.answer: Kill his brother.

questions.question: Why was Esau so angry?
questions.answer: Jacob had stolen his blessing.

questions.question: What did Rebekah tell Jacob to do?
questions.answer: Go and live with her brother, Laban.

questions.question: How long did Rebekah tell Jacob to stay at her brother Laban's house?
questions.answer: Until she sent a message to say that Esau had calmed down.

questions.question: Why?
questions.answer: Cars and planes hadn't been invented yet!

questions.question: What did he use instead?
questions.answer: A stone.

questions.question: What happened to Jacob as he slept under the stars that night?
questions.answer: He had a dream.

questions.question: How high did it reach?
questions.answer: All the way to heaven.

questions.question: Who was on it?
questions.answer: Angels.

questions.question: What were the angels doing on Jacob's sky-high dream stairs?
questions.answer: Going up and down.

questions.question: Who was standing at the top of the angel-covered ladder in Jacob's dream?
questions.answer: The Lord God.

questions.question: What did God look like to Jacob?
questions.answer: The Bible doesn't say.
questions.notes: Answer is provided in the source narrative immediately following the question; not printed in parentheses.

questions.question: Where have you heard those words before?
questions.answer: God made those same promises to Abraham and Isaac.

questions.question: What did Jacob say after he woke up?
questions.answer: God was in this place and I didn't even know it!

questions.question: Who would be scared of an angel-covered ladder to heaven?
questions.notes: Source uses a rhetorical or open question; no printed parenthetical answer.

questions.question: But is "holy" a good word to describe Jacob?
questions.answer: No way!
questions.notes: Answer is provided in the source narrative immediately following the question; not printed in parentheses.

questions.question: What had Jacob done that showed he wasn't holy?
questions.answer: Fooled his father, stolen Esau's blessing.

questions.question: What did he do?
questions.answer: Stood up the stone.

questions.question: What else did Jacob do to treat his stone pillow in a special way?
questions.answer: Poured olive oil over it.

questions.question: What promise did Jacob make?
questions.answer: If you'll be with me, then you'll be my God.

questions.question: So if God blessed him with ten sheep, how many would he give as a sacrifice to God?
So, how does the story of Jacob’s dream teach us, strengthen us, encourage us, or give us hope?
questions.notes: Source uses a rhetorical or open question; no printed parenthetical answer.

questions.question: What were those promises again?
questions.answer: To grow him into a great nation, give his people a great land, and use his family to bless the whole world.

questions.question: Who?
questions.answer: Jesus.

questions.question: What did he do to save the world from their sins?
questions.answer: Died on a cross, rose from the dead.

questions.question: Are they still alive and walking around the earth today?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: guess who will be there in that kingdom with us?
questions.answer: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob!

questions.question: What does ladder climbing (or stair climbing) have to do with today’s story?
questions.answer: Jacob’s dream of a ladder to the sky.

questions.question: What did Esau plan to do to Jacob? Why?
questions.answer: Kill him for stealing his blessing

questions.question: Where did Jacob’s parents send him? Why?
questions.answer: To his uncle Laban’s to hide from Esau

questions.question: What did Jacob use for his pillow?
questions.answer: A stone

questions.question: What did Jacob see in his dream?
questions.answer: A ladder/stairway to heaven, angels going up and down

questions.question: Who was standing at the top of the ladder/stairway in Jacob’s dream?
questions.answer: God

questions.question: What did God say to Jacob in the dream?
questions.answer: He gave Jacob the same promises he made to Abraham

questions.question: What did Jacob do with the stone after the dream?
questions.answer: Stood it up, poured oil on it

questions.question: What promise did Jacob make to God?
questions.answer: If you’ll be with me, then you will be my God

questions.question: Jacob called that place “Bethel.” What did Bethel mean?
questions.answer: House of God

questions.question: What special name did we learn for God today?
questions.answer: The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob

facts.statement: Esau was angry enough to threaten Jacob.
Esau congratulated Jacob on receiving the blessing.
Jacob went to stay with his uncle Laban.
Jacob traveled to Egypt to hide from Esau.
Jacob used a stone as a pillow when he slept outdoors.
Jacob slept in a palace on the way to Laban.
Jacob dreamed of a stairway that reached heaven.
Angels were climbing up and down the stairway.
Jacob saw sheep climbing the stairway in his dream.
God repeated the promises he had made to Abraham.
God said He would leave Jacob alone on his journey.
Jacob realized the Lord was in that place.
Jacob named the place where he dreamed Jericho.
Jacob stood up his stone pillow as a special marker.
Jacob poured olive oil over the stone.
Jacob threw the stone away and forgot the dream.
Jacob promised to give God one tenth of what he received.
Jacob promised that the Lord would be his God.
Jacob vowed never to pray to God again.
Bethel means “house of God.”
Jacob hoped his brother Esau would never calm down.
God promised to watch over Jacob wherever he went.

clues.text: I slept with my head on a stone and dreamed about a stairway to heaven.
I was angry that my twin brother took my blessing.
I was the uncle whose home Jacob was traveling to.
I told Jacob to stay with my brother until Esau calmed down.

reviewFlags.text: The source quotes Matthew 22:31-32, ESV, ending with an ellipsis. All seven verse activities currently retain this original text. Teacher must choose and verify the exact BSB excerpt and synchronize all verse-linked activity fields in Review Studio.

Review selected linked canonical True/False, Maze and Sort facts, especially suggested false statements. No fact ID is reused across those three activities.
Odd Words and Checkboxes use plausible Bible-story distractors rather than arbitrary modern objects. Confirm they are not relevant to this particular lesson and appropriate for the students.

Review the six deliberate errors in Circle the Mistakes and the 11-blank Finish the Story narrative. Review story-order wording and distinct complete drawing captions for clarity, precision and source fidelity.

Preserve both original Important Idea statements and source wording. Teacher should review lessons about Esau’s threatened violence, Jacob’s deception, holiness, the promise to Abraham/Isaac/Jacob, giving a tenth, and the connection to Jesus.

Verify that crossword words actually interlock, word searches place every word, cryptograms generate, and SVG/PDF output fits, including all three numbered worksheet presets. Local character checks are not equivalent to a generator pass.
